headline: Medium-risk pair: PaddleOCR can ingest documents/images while langchain4j can mediate outputs, creating default-path leakage and cascading-error exposure; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel or direct ingestion path is documented between langchain4j and PaddleOCR, so prompt injection is not a default-path risk. The only plausible bridge is manual or orchestrated handoff of OCR text into langchain4j, which is unusual and not evidenced here. Uncertainty keeps this above none but below medium.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies PaddleOCR OCR text into langchain4j prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Strip instructions from OCR text before passing it onward.
Use a fixed prompt template with quoted OCR content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all OCR outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images and has allowlisted network egress plus API calls, so sensitive file contents can leave the local boundary. langchain4j has no network egress, but it can still receive and transform those contents, making the pair a default-path leakage concern when documents contain secrets or personal data. The shared-data pathway is plausible even without explicit shared storage details.
conditions: IF documents or images contain secrets, personal data, or regulated records, leakage impact increases.
IF PaddleOCR sends extracted content to external APIs, data leaves the local environment.
mitigations: Restrict input to non-sensitive documents.
Disable external API calls in PaddleOCR workflows.
Redact sensitive fields before OCR.
Separate OCR output storage from downstream prompts.
requires-engineering: enforce per-document data classification gates.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: langchain4j exposes no write or network surface in the profile, while PaddleOCR has allowlisted egress and browser capability. That creates some operational overlap only if an orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable resource, which is not shown here. Because the conflicting write surface is absent from the profiles, this stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same filesystem or database, conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, race conditions become plausible.
mitigations: Avoid shared writable directories.
Serialize any shared-state updates.
Use separate service accounts.
Check for lock files before writes.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces document-derived text and langchain4j can consume and rephrase it, so A-to-B style cascading errors are plausible if OCR output is treated as authoritative. The profiles do not show verification or provenance checks, so hallucinated or misread text can propagate into downstream work products. This is a default-path quality risk rather than a direct action-taking hazard.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is used as source text for summaries, decisions, or tickets, errors can cascade.
IF langchain4j is prompted to trust OCR output without verification, propagation risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review of OCR outputs.
Compare OCR text against the source image for critical fields.
Use confidence thresholds before downstream use.
Quote OCR text verbatim in prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance and verification metadata.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. PaddleOCR touches documents and images, but there is no evidence of PHI, EU-only data, or conflicting compliance controls. Because the relevant compliance surfaces are not specified, only a low residual risk remains.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are processed, compliance review is required.
IF deployment policies impose retention or residency constraints, the pair must be checked against them.
mitigations: Classify input data before processing.
Avoid regulated data in this workflow.
Document retention settings.
Confirm residency requirements for any external API use.
requires-engineering: map the workflow to a formal compliance control set.
